answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable credential before it can transact, like a merchant dyeing goods with saffron pigment that cannot be faked cheaply. Identities accumulate reputation only through completed work over time, and a shared onyx ledger records every credential issuance so duplicates are visible to all. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs more than any gain, because each fake must earn its own history, pay its own stake, and pass the same public checks as a real agent.
